name: Guardian genius crossword No 165
preamble: Eight solutions (four being of two words) comprise 6 across 29, which is clued without definition. Of the other clues, four across and four down contain superfluous words or phrases that provide either definitions or wordplay for the themed eight. The remaining eight definitions or wordplay are: board, deck games, fish, notes, religious image, song, supporter and World Cup winners.

solutions.check: grid and clues read from the Guardian's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; each light's entry one fifteensquared prints for it, the only choice of them whose crossings all agree; an entry not its answer carries the answer as its alteration's `from`

clue.text: Work for two solid hours at first in nude … to endless delight

indicators.note: something endless has lost its final part, so the last letter goes
at first points to the opening letter of each of the words before it
one thing set in another sits inside it

blocks.note: joy is delight
bare means naked
the initial letters of solid and hours

explanation.surface: A cheeky pep talk: put in two hours' solid graft naked and you'll find bliss.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis is surface punctuation only; 'endless' trims the word after it, not the one before.
explanation.definitionFit: A job share is one post split between two employees, each working part of the hours.

clue.text: Stop filming lovely short conductor

indicators.note: a word cut short is missing its tail, so drop the final letter

blocks.note: cute means lovely or attractive
superfluous word: the definition for the themed entry at 3 down

explanation.surface: A film shoot halted because the conductor in the orchestra scene is too handsome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conductor' is one of the puzzle's superfluous words: it is the definition of the themed SOLTI at 3 down, whose own clue is not printed.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Cut!' is the director's call to halt the camera, so it is the instruction to end a take.

clue.text: Open land to the north providing space — a function of the countryside

indicators.note: in a down clue, heading north means reading from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: a moor is open, uncultivated upland
superfluous phrase: the definition for the themed entry at 13 across

explanation.surface: A note on how northern moorland gives breathing room, a service the countryside provides.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a function of the countryside' is superfluous: it defines the themed HUNT BALL at 13 across, whose own clue is not printed.
explanation.definitionFit: Room means available space, as in there is no room to move.

clue.text: Half-heartedly plug double money game, initially showing annoyance

indicators.note: doing something half-heartedly means losing part of the heart, the middle of the word
double asks for the same piece written twice in a row
initially points to the opening letter of the word before it

blocks.note: to tout is to plug or push something for sale
tin is slang for money
first letter of game

explanation.surface: Advertising a money game unenthusiastically while looking irritated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-heartedly' removes the middle letter of the four-letter word, and 'double' then writes the shortened piece twice.
explanation.definitionFit: To tut-tut is to click the tongue in disapproval, so tut-tutting is expressing irritation.

clue.text: With money invested, assuming five hundred's a thousand

indicators.note: money invested is put inside something, so these letters go within another word
read as 'is', it says one thing now stands as another, so one letter is swapped for a new one

blocks.note: taking on, as in assuming a role
W is the standard abbreviation for with
oof is old slang for money
G, short for grand, is a thousand pounds
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred

explanation.surface: A financier's sum: once cash is put in, five hundred turns into a thousand.
explanation.walkthrough: Oof is dated British slang. G for grand, the final letter, becomes D, the Roman five hundred. The preamble says this entry has no definition: it names the theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Each themed entry is a matching pair, two fish, two notes, two prime ministers, so a pair of the same sort.

clue.text: One laughing about Welsh bird

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece wraps round another

blocks.note: someone who titters is laughing
W is the abbreviation for Welsh

explanation.surface: Someone giggling at a bird from Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: TITTERER goes round W after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A twitterer is a creature that twitters, and twittering is the chirping of small birds.

clue.text: Sharp practice over Anfield difficult to expose

indicators.note: exposing something reveals what was inside, so the letters are already in the clue
in a down clue, over means turned upside down, read bottom to top

blocks.note: the letters run across the two words, starting inside Anfield

explanation.surface: Exposing cheating at Liverpool's ground proves hard.
explanation.walkthrough: Anfield is Liverpool FC's football stadium. Read the run of letters upwards for the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiddle is a swindle or dishonest dealing, which is what sharp practice means.

clue.text: Men get cold feet during attack — too much to lose in extremis

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its ends, so keep only the outside letters
something during an event happens inside it, so these letters go within

blocks.note: superfluous word: the wordplay for the themed entry at 23 across
a bout is a fit or attack of illness
OTT, over the top, means excessive
the first and last letters of lose

explanation.surface: Faced with a fight, the troops lose their nerve; things are too much to bear at the extreme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Men' is superfluous: it is the wordplay for the themed PATRON at 23 across, the names PAT and RON. OTT is British shorthand for over the top.
explanation.definitionFit: To bottle out is British slang for losing your nerve and backing away from something.

clue.text: One's struggle in the past with climbers crossing

blocks.note: one is I, the Roman numeral; the 's joins it to what follows
vied is the past tense of vie, to struggle or compete
superfluous word: the definition for the themed entry at 19 across

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a past struggle alongside fellow mountaineers on a traverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' is superfluous: it defines the themed PONTOON BRIDGE at 19 across. 'Climbers' here are climbing plants, not mountaineers.
explanation.definitionFit: Ivied means covered in ivy, a climbing plant, so overgrown with creepers.

clue.text: Domestic goddess is the new Nigella, ultimately

indicators.note: something new is remade, so those words are rearranged
ultimately points to the final letter of the word before it

blocks.note: these letters rearranged
last letter of Nigella

explanation.surface: Hailing a TV cook as the latest 'domestic goddess', the label famously attached to Nigella Lawson.
explanation.walkthrough: Nigella Lawson is a British TV cook whose book title made 'domestic goddess' her tag; here the phrase is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Hestia is the Greek goddess of the hearth and home, literally a deity of the household.

clue.text: Pinch money when Miss goes out

indicators.note: one thing going outside another wraps around it

blocks.note: to skip is to miss out
M is the abbreviation for money

explanation.surface: Someone steals cash when the lady of the house steps out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pinch money' looks like one idea, theft; only 'Pinch' defines, in the sense of being stingy.
explanation.definitionFit: To skimp is to economise meanly, the same sense as to pinch pennies.

clue.text: Note to self — second drink also spiked

indicators.note: a spiked drink has something slipped into it

blocks.note: me is oneself
a mo is a moment, a second
rum is a spirit
and means also

explanation.surface: A reminder to yourself: your second drink was also doctored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note to self' reads as one phrase, but only 'Note' defines; a mo is British for a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A memorandum is a written note recording something to be remembered.

clue.text: Auntie talks with Eric — the result's affected European agreements

indicators.note: affected means altered or acted upon, so the letters are changed round

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
superfluous phrase: the wordplay for the themed entry at 7 down

explanation.surface: Brexit news: the talks with a negotiator have upset European agreements.
explanation.walkthrough: Auntie is the BBC's nickname. 'European agreements' is superfluous: it is the wordplay for the themed OUIJA at 7 down, French OUI plus German JA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Reith Lectures are an annual series of radio talks broadcast by the BBC.

clue.text: Give way over one department's balancing act

blocks.note: to hand is to give
St is the abbreviation for street, a way
an means one
D abbreviates department; the 's links it to the definition

explanation.surface: An office manager yields, over the department's juggling of priorities.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'over' simply sets the first pieces above the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A handstand is a gymnastic feat of balancing upside down on the hands.

clue.text: Where Thomas lives is very clean, right?

blocks.note: so means very
to do a room is to clean it
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Asking whether Thomas's home is spotless.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas is Thomas the Tank Engine, the children's-book railway character.
explanation.definitionFit: Sodor is the fictional island in the Railway Series books where Thomas the Tank Engine runs.

clue.text: Destroying love letters, finished with new friend in spring

indicators.note: destroying something removes it entirely from the word that follows

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis, the letter O
superfluous word: the wordplay for the themed entry at 26 across
over means finished
N is the abbreviation for new
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: Burning old love letters, done with them, with a new friend in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: OVER loses its O; 'letters' is superfluous, the wordplay for the themed PIETA at 26 across, the Greek letters PI and ETA.
explanation.definitionFit: Vernal means relating to spring, so vernally means in a springlike way or season.

clue.text: More work leading to jams — road's up

indicators.note: to jam is to squeeze into a space, so one piece goes inside
in a down clue, up means read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: up means ahead, as a team two goals up
taken as written
the A1 is Britain's main north road, with 1 as I

explanation.surface: Extra labour ahead because of traffic jams where the road is dug up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More' is Sir Thomas More, not extra. The A1 is Britain's longest numbered road, London to Edinburgh.
explanation.definitionFit: Utopia is the 1516 book by Sir Thomas More describing an ideal island society.

clue.text: African prime ministers head back home — is a struggle fitting in

indicators.note: going back means reading from right to left
letters in a struggle are tossed about into a new order
fitting in means being put inside another word

blocks.note: superfluous phrase: the wordplay for the themed entry at 30 across
nut is slang for head
in means at home
these letters rearranged

explanation.surface: African leaders return home and find it hard to settle in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prime ministers' is superfluous: it is the wordplay for the themed MAGGIE MAY at 30 across, Thatcher and Theresa May.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tunisian is a native of Tunisia, a country in North Africa.

clue.text: Russian about to arrest English moles

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, so the name is read backwards
arresting someone holds them, so one piece is held inside

blocks.note: Ivan is a typical Russian man's name
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A Russian is about to detain English spies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moles' looks like spies but means birthmarks. IVAN reversed holds E.
explanation.definitionFit: Naevi is the plural of naevus, a birthmark or mole on the skin.

clue.text: Countryman's a picky eater — in perfect shape, consuming almost nothing

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
consuming means taking inside

blocks.note: superfluous phrase: the definition for the themed entry at 1 across
A1 means first-class, with 1 as I
zero is nothing

explanation.surface: A fussy-eating compatriot stays fit by eating next to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a picky eater' is superfluous: it defines the themed JACK SPRAT at 1 across, the nursery-rhyme man who could eat no fat. A1 is the old term for a first-class ship, so excellent.
explanation.definitionFit: An Azeri is a native of Azerbaijan, a fellow citizen of that country.

clue.text: Very keen to see past end of building

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter

blocks.note: ago means in the past
last letter of building

explanation.surface: Someone eager to look beyond a building's far end.
explanation.definitionFit: Agog means eagerly excited, on the edge of one's seat.

clue.text: After training, golden boy enters boxer's quarters?

indicators.note: training reshapes something, so the word is rearranged
entering means going inside

blocks.note: these letters rearranged
Ken is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A gilded young fighter moves into the boxing camp's accommodation after training.
explanation.walkthrough: The boxer is the dog breed, not a fighter; the question mark flags that.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog kennel is a shelter for a dog, and a boxer is a breed of dog.

clue.text: Picked up crew where Americans fought, briefly

indicators.note: in a down clue, picked up means lifted, so read bottom to top

blocks.note: to man a ship is to crew it

explanation.surface: A unit was recruited for the war in Vietnam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up' tempts as a sound signal, but here it means lifted upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Nam is American slang shortening of Vietnam, scene of the Vietnam War.

clue.text: See 6
